content: The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly affected the mental health of individuals with diabetes. People living with diabetes have experienced elevated levels of psychological distress, driven by factors such as prolonged isolation, heightened anxiety about the risk of infection, and limitations on social interactions. These mental health challenges are particularly severe among older adults with diabetes, who are also more likely to struggle with feelings of loneliness. There has been a notable increase in the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and symptoms related to stress among this population. These issues are largely attributed to the ongoing restrictions imposed during the pandemic, a reduction in physical activity levels, and disruptions to normal dietary routines. Furthermore, many individuals with diabetes have encountered significant obstacles in maintaining a consistent and healthy lifestyle, which has negatively influenced their ability to manage their condition effectively and has diminished their overall quality of life.
